pins.definition: To move through water by moving your body.
To move through water by moving parts of the body.
To move through water by using body movements.

situation: A lone man in traditional clothes moves steadily through a wide, open river, using his arms and legs to propel himself forward.
subject: the act of moving through water
brief: A man is in mid-stroke in the middle of a flowing river, his limbs positioned to show the continuous motion of propelling himself through the water. Ripples and currents wrap around his body, and water droplets scatter from his reaching hand.
prompt: A man is in mid-stroke in the middle of a flowing river, his limbs positioned to show the continuous motion of propelling himself through the water. Ripples and currents wrap around his body, and water droplets scatter from his reaching hand. a Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print, flat layered colour planes, Prussian blue and vermilion, visible woodgrain and registration edges, weather and motion stylised into pattern. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
